doc.title: Bill Allred interviewed by Monk Rowe, Orlando, Florida, February 24, 2017

title: Trad jazz as an art form and New Orleans brass bands
summary: Rowe suggests trad is dismissed as too happy; Allred mentions the Onward Brass Band and a wedding request.

venues.name: International Association of Jazz Educators conference

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: Years ago I attended the International Association of Jazz Educators, big huge organization, and thousands of people come to these events. And they had a panel discussion that said “Trad Jazz is Alive and Well.” Well the people on the panel didn’t really believe it I think, and not only that, with all the performances during the weekend there was no trad jazz. And I personally think it’s because the music is — most of the time — very upbeat and happy and thus it doesn’t — it’s not looked on as a real art form. It’s too darn happy. And that’s just my own personal feeling about it.

No I can see where you — now there’s this other whole avenue of like the New Orleans guys, the Onward Brass Band and this, where they combine blues, rock & roll, trad, and marching around, and kind of carrying the banner of New Orleans, and that’s good. I had a narrow escape one time because this girl said, “Oh do you guys play New Orleans jazz?” I said, “Yeah.” You know. And she said, “Well we’d like you to play our wedding. Right after we get married we want to march down the street or something, to this hotel.” And we come up with a price, they had money to spend. She said, “I’ll send you a tape of some of the stuff I like.” And it was all this very Onward Brass Band Stuff and we managed to learn a couple of things. So that’s another whole different thing. But at least it’s doing it.
